svg.text: AIRLINE BOOKING — SEAT HOLD (CAS + TTL) FLOW
Flight AI-202. 12A is AVAILABLE. Same millisecond:
T1 vs T2 contend on ONE AtomicReference
T3 touches a different reference → truly parallel
no global lock, so contention is per SEAT,
not per flight and certainly not per airline
14C has its own AtomicReference — zero waiting
if (!eligible) return false // BOOKED, or a live hold
// lost the race — re-read and re-check eligibility
the hold is the ticket to a later confirm()
daemon thread → JVM can still exit; close() stops it
LAZY — tryHold walks over the corpse
an expired HELD counts as eligible,
so the next booker CASes straight over it
⇒ the sweeper is an OPTIMISATION, not a
correctness dependency. Miss a tick, nothing breaks. ✓
BOOKING LIFECYCLE — every transition also moves the seat slot
holdSeat: CAS AVAILABLE → HELD, PNR issued
expire() on a CONFIRMED booking ⇒ IllegalStateException
ConfirmedState refuses it — a paid seat can never be swept away.
The sweeper only ever touches slots still in HELD.
Slot and booking move together, always in this order:
1. CAS the seat slot (the contended resource)
2. only if the CAS won, transition the Booking state
Honest gap: steps 1 and 2 are not one atomic unit. A crash
between them leaves a BOOKED slot with a HELD booking —
in-process that window is invisible; across a DB you'd need
one transaction or a reconciling job.
release() checks the PNR, so a stale caller cannot free someone else's seat.

g.text: Payment takes seconds and can fail.
the seat with no expiry means one
A TTL hold is the middle ground: exclusive
Occupancy is a fresh immutable object
on every transition, and CAS compares
by REFERENCE. A slot that went
so the stale CAS correctly fails.

svg.text: ① three threads, one seat → ② the tryHold CAS loop and its eligibility test → ③ TTL: eager sweeper + lazy CAS-over-expired → ④ HELD → CONFIRMED / CANCELLED / EXPIRED, and what each does to the seat slot

g.text: ① A seat slot has at most one live owner.
② Only the owning PNR may release or confirm.
③ An expired hold is indistinguishable from free.
Lock-free per-seat AtomicReference<Occupancy> · hold TTL · daemon sweeper — LLD
